correctness.rationale: Uniform ordered endpoints induce uniform perfect matchings; component boundaries correspond exactly to internally matched prefixes. Conditioning on a prefix cut splits the matching into independent blocks and removes \(2k(n-k)/3\) expected edges. Summing this exact decrement gives the covariance. A two-edge overlap calculation yields Var(E)=n(n-1)(2n+1)/45, and joint-cut probabilities and endpoint bounds yield Var(C)=1/n+O(n^-2) and the -sqrt(10)/n correlation. Exhaustive rational checks for 2<=n<=7 agree with the formulas. The proof does not extrapolate finite enumeration to infinity.

broader_coverage.reasoning: High-probability connectivity and unconditional edge density are separate marginals and imply neither the finite covariance formula nor its nonvanishing limit. Covered length depends on endpoint spacings, whereas the graph edge count depends only on endpoint ranks. The accessible alternative interval-service-system model has different sampling and does not subsume uniform independent endpoint pairing.

value.rationale: The component count is a fundamental topological descriptor, and edge count is a fundamental density descriptor of the canonical interval graph. The all-n distribution-free exact negative covariance and asymptotic persistence distinguish the full mixed law from the separate connectivity and density results. The exceptional rare event probability is 1/n+O(n^-2), yet covariance approaches -2/3, and the exact covariance with Var(E) and Var(C) yields the sharp -sqrt(10)/n correlation rate. This is a motivated, reusable graph-statistic calibration, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
